items.criterion: Before the run writes the convention, it names the subject and why the subject is important now. Then it asks one question. The question has two or three options, each with a real example from wordfreq, and one recommended option with a reason.
With `defaults`, the run asks no question and takes its recommended option. It marks the choice as assumed in a file that the user can read.
The design spec has the form of the design template. A new spec is a new file in `pdlc/specs/design/`. A changed spec is the existing file, edited in place, with `Default: no`.
The user gets a rule that a later stage can apply with no guess. The rule is the option that the user agreed to, or the recommended option with `defaults`.
The user gets exactly one migration intent for each job or capability whose code breaks the agreed rule. Code that already obeys the rule gets no migration intent.
Each intent that the run adds is a file from the intent template, in the form of the inbox-files adapter. Each migration intent has the name "Migrate <spec> to <convention>".
The run does not start the intents, and does not migrate any code. The user selects when each intent runs.
The run commits all its work on main, in one commit with the subject `Convention DES-<name>`.
The closing message tells the user how many migration intents the run added. It also says that the user selects when each intent runs.
The design spec has requirements for the convention, with the status `proposed`. The run adds one intent to build the check.
